result.description:
Location: Woolner NT, with work across the Northern Territory
Employment Type: Full-time
Hours: 38 hours per week
Salary: AUD $69,000 to $89,000 per annum plus superannuation, depending on skills and experience

About Us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the Employer
The business (ABN 53 603 812 004) is a Darwin-based specialist HVAC hygiene company providing cleaning, inspection and maintenance services for commercial and industrial air conditioning systems, ductwork, commercial kitchen exhaust systems, cool rooms and mould-affected environments throughout the Northern Territory. Our clients include commercial, industrial, Defence and government organisations requiring specialist indoor air quality and HVAC hygiene services.  

We are looking for a reliable HVAC Cleaning Technician (High Access) to join our team.

About the Role
The HVAC Cleaning Technician (High Access) will carry out specialist cleaning, maintenance and inspection work on HVAC systems located in commercial, industrial and high-access environments. The role routinely involves safely accessing rooftop plant, elevated work areas and other difficult-to-reach locations using approved ladders, elevated work platforms and other approved height access equipment. 

The successful applicant will:
- Safely access rooftop plant, elevated mechanical services, ceiling spaces and other difficult-to-reach work areas using ladders, fall-arrest systems, elevated work platforms (EWPs), scissor lifts and other approved height access equipment to perform specialist HVAC cleaning, inspection and maintenance activities.
- Carry out specialised cleaning and hygiene services for commercial and industrial HVAC systems, ductwork and ventilation systems.
- Clean air handling units (AHUs), plant rooms, supply and return air ducts, evaporator coils, condenser units, filters and associated HVAC equipment.
- Perform commercial kitchen exhaust system cleaning, including hoods, ductwork, fans and associated ventilation equipment.
- Clean cool rooms, ventilation equipment and other specialist environments to maintain hygiene and operational standards.
- Assist with mould remediation and microbial cleaning projects in accordance with company procedures.
- Conduct pre-start inspections of elevated work areas, identify potential hazards and implement appropriate safety controls before commencing work. 
- Operate specialist cleaning equipment, including pressure cleaning equipment, HEPA vacuum systems and other industry-specific cleaning tools.
- Take photographs, complete digital job records, inspection reports and service documentation for completed works.
- Maintain company vehicles, tools, equipment and personal protective equipment in a safe and serviceable condition.
- Work professionally with clients, contractors and other team members while maintaining the company's high standards of workmanship and customer service.

Applicants should have:
- Experience in commercial HVAC cleaning, industrial cleaning, building maintenance, duct cleaning, ventilation system cleaning, or a similar hands-on trade or technical environment.
- Demonstrated ability and confidence to safely work at heights in commercial and industrial environments while complying with WHS requirements. 
- Experience using ladders, elevated work platforms (EWP), scissor lifts or other approved height access equipment will be highly regarded.
- Ability to operate pressure cleaning equipment, HEPA vacuum systems and other specialist cleaning equipment.
- Good physical fitness and the ability to perform manual work in commercial and industrial environments.
- Ability to read and follow work instructions, safe work procedures and site-specific requirements.
- Basic computer or mobile device skills to complete digital job records, inspection reports and photographic documentation.
- Good communication skills and the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a small team.
- A strong work ethic, attention to detail and commitment to delivering high-quality workmanship and customer service.
- Comfortable working on rooftops, elevated mechanical plant and other high-access locations as part of normal day-to-day duties. 

Applicants should have:
- Current Working at Heights certificate, or willingness to obtain prior to commencement
- Current driver licence.
- Current NT White Card or equivalent
- Elevated Work Platform licence or demonstrated experience operating EWP will be highly regarded
- Confined Space or First Aid training, or other relevant safety training preferred.

How to Apply
We are looking for motivated and reliable people who enjoy practical work and take pride in delivering high-quality HVAC hygiene, cleaning and maintenance services.  

To apply, please submit:
- A current resume outlining your relevant work experience and the contact details of two referees.
- A cover letter (maximum 600 words) addressing the following:
- Why you are applying for this position.
- An example of when you demonstrated excellent customer service, initiative or teamwork (using the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action and Result).
- How your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of this role.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a practical, professional team delivering specialist HVAC hygiene, duct cleaning, kitchen exhaust cleaning, mould remediation and commercial cleaning services across the Northern Territory, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Walk-in or telephone enquiries regarding this vacancy will not be accepted.

Applications close: 1 August 2026

result.description:
Global Vision Recruitment on behalf of Flair & Fine Care Pty Ltd

Date Posted: 20 July 2026

Position: Residential Care Officer 

Salary: $79,500 - $85,000 per annum plus 12% superannuation

Hours: 38 hours per week

Employment Type: Full-time

Location: 2 Vernon Street, Huntingdale VIC 3166

Experience required: Minimum 1 year of relevant experience in disability support, supported independent living, residential care, or a similar care environment

About the Business

Flair & Fine Care Pty Ltd is a trusted NDIS provider dedicated to empowering individuals to live independently and achieve their personal goals. We deliver high-quality, person-centred support services tailored to the unique needs of people living with disability. Our services include Supported Independent Living (SIL), community participation, personal care, life skills development, and capacity-building support, with a strong focus on promoting independence, inclusion, dignity, and wellbeing.

We are seeking a compassionate and experienced Residential Care Officer to join our team and provide high-quality support to residents living in supported accommodation while fostering a safe, respectful, and empowering home environment.

Key Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

•	Conduct assessments of resident’s individual needs, strengths, preferences, and personal goals, and assist in implementing person-centred support plans that promote independence, wellbeing, and capacity building. 

•	Provide day-to-day care, supervision, and practical support to residents living in supported accommodation, assisting with personal care, household routines, daily living activities, and the development of essential life skills. 

•	Observe, monitor, and document resident’s physical, emotional, and behavioural wellbeing, maintaining accurate progress notes and reporting significant changes to the appropriate supervisors and support teams. 

•	Recognise when resident’s require additional therapeutic, medical, or community-based services and facilitate appropriate referrals in collaboration with support coordinators and allied health professionals. 

•	Build positive relationships with residents, families, guardians, healthcare professionals, and external service providers to ensure coordinated, person-centred support and continuity of care. 

•	Encourage and support residents to engage in community, recreational, educational, and social activities that enhance inclusion, confidence, independence, and overall quality of life. 

•	Implement individual behaviour support strategies and respond appropriately to incidents or challenging behaviours in accordance with approved behaviour support plans, organisational policies, and NDIS Practice Standards. 

•	Foster a safe, respectful, and inclusive home environment that upholds resident’s rights, promotes dignity, encourages choice and independence, and respects cultural diversity and individual preferences. 

•	Maintain accurate client records, case notes, incident reports, and support documentation while ensuring all services are delivered in compliance with organisational policies, NDIS Practice Standards, safeguarding requirements, and workplace health and safety legislation. 

•	Work collaboratively with colleagues and participate in team meetings, training, and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance the quality and consistency of support services provided to residents.

Qualifications

•	Relevant qualification in Individual Support, Community Services, Disability, Mental Health, or a related field. 

•	Minimum 1 year of relevant experience in disability support, supported independent living, residential care, or a similar care environment. 

Skills & Other Requirements

•	Demonstrated experience supporting people living with disability in residential or supported accommodation settings. 

•	Strong understanding of person-centred care principles, NDIS Practice Standards, and safeguarding requirements. 

•	Excellent interpersonal, communication, and relationship-building skills. 

•	Ability to manage challenging behaviours with empathy, professionalism, and sound judgement. 

•	Strong organisational, record-keeping, and problem-solving abilities. 

•	Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team. 

•	Commitment to maintaining confidentiality, professionalism, and high standards of care. 

•	Current First Aid and CPR certification (or willingness to obtain), NDIS Worker Screening Check, and Working with Children Check (where applicable). 

If you are passionate about supporting people with disability to live fulfilling and independent lives, we encourage you to apply for this rewarding opportunity with Flair & Fine Care Pty Ltd.

Interested applicants may submit their application to recruit@gvrc.com.au. Please note that only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

result.description: Astern Group Pty Ltd   ASTERN GROUP PTY LTD  is seeking to employ a full-time Construction Project Manager.  You will need to work 38 hours per week. You will responsible for aiding the project staff during the construction stages of infrastructure projects The successful candidate will be responsible for the daily management, supervision, coordination, and successful delivery of civil infrastructure construction projects. This role requires strong project management skills, including contract administration, scheduling, estimating, procurement, budgeting, and stakeholder management, while ensuring projects are delivered safely, on time, within budget, and to the required quality standards.                          Benefits   Competitive salary package with opportunities for career progression.   Long-term employment with a growing civil construction company.   Diverse and challenging projects   Supportive leadership team with an open-door culture.   Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.   Modern equipment, technology and systems to help you succeed.   Collaborative team environment where your contribution is valued.   Strong commitment to safety, quality and employee wellbeing.   Recognition and reward for high performance and commitment.    Task & responsibilities  The Construction Project Manager will be responsible for:   Interpreting construction drawings, specifications and contract documentation.  Planning, coordinating and managing construction projects from commencement through to completion.  Developing, implementing and monitoring project construction programs.  Procuring project materials, subcontractors, plant and equipment.  Managing project budgets and ensuring projects are completed within approved financial targets.  Monitoring project progress and ensuring milestones are achieved on schedule.  Ensuring all pre-construction requirements are completed prior to project commencement.  Managing labour resources and subcontractors to meet project objectives.  Ensuring projects are delivered in accordance with the latest approved drawings, specifications and schedules.  Coordinating the timely delivery of plant, equipment and hired materials in consultation with the Plant Manager.  Maintaining comprehensive and up-to-date project records and contract documentation.  Preparing project reports, progress claims, contract notifications and variation claims in accordance with contractual requirements.  Managing project timelines through accurate and regularly updated construction and contract programs.  Preparing and submitting updated project documentation to relevant authorities upon project completion to achieve Practical Completion (PC).  Ensuring strict compliance with company policies, and project management procedures.  Monitoring project costs and implementing corrective actions where budget variations occur.  Ensuring all variation works receive written client approval before commencement.  Liaising with engineers, consultants, clients, subcontractors, suppliers and other technical professionals.  Ensuring project personnel and contractors are appropriately qualified, experienced and perform efficiently within their assigned responsibilities.  Reviewing and approving employee timesheets and ensuring required project documentation is submitted to Payroll, Accounts Payable and Office Administration. Job description:

 
Join an evolving recruitment team to provide high-quality, end-to-end recruitment support, working closely with hiring managers and stakeholders to deliver efficient and effective recruitment outcomes across the Department of Health.

 

 






 

The Team

Recruitment Services is implementing a new statewide operating model and structure designed to strengthen recruitment capability, improve consistency, and support a more modern end-to-end service across the Department of Health. We're building a stronger, more specialised team to support consistent end-to-end recruitment across the Department, and we're recruiting to multiple roles as part of this implementation.

Why this is a great time to join

You'll join an evolving, statewide team that is improving how recruitment works in practice - standardising workflows, lifting capability, and using technology more effectively to support managers and candidates. This is an opportunity to have real impact at scale, contribute to continuous improvement, and help attract the workforce that supports health services across Tasmania, leading to stronger Tasmanian community. 

The Role

As a Recruitment Officer, you will support the end-to-end recruitment process by:

Engaging with stakeholders with a client and customer focus, providing timely and friendly support.

Coordinating recruitment administration activities from advertising through to appointment.

Maintaining accurate and confidential records within e-Recruitment and HR systems.

Monitoring recruitment workflows and assisting the team to meet service delivery timeframes.

Responding to recruitment enquiries and providing advice through the People and Culture Portal.

Preparing and distributing recruitment and selection documentation.

Drafting applicant communications and ensuring candidates receive timely updates.

Publishing job advertisements across approved recruitment platforms.

Processing establishment changes and minor position amendments.

Supporting continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to enhance recruitment processes and services.

Providing general administrative support to the Recruitment team as required.

You will need

Knowledge of, and-or experience within a human resources or recruitment operational environment and in the use of human resource management systems, applicant tracking systems, technical tools or databases particularly in the areas of recruitment or demonstrated capability to develop such knowledge within a reasonable timeframe.

Knowledge of, and experience in the application of recruitment practices, procedures and legislation or a demonstrated capability to develop such knowledge within a reasonable timeframe.

Well-developed interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain operational procedures and provide information to, and liaise with, clients, stakeholders and members of the public.

Note: - Please refer to the Statement of Duties for all the selection criteria of this position to address in your application.

Details of appointment

Permanent full time, day worker position, working 76 hours per fortnight.

*Notwithstanding hours to be negotiated with the successful applicant.

Applicants should note that, for a period of twelve months from the date of publication, this selection process may be used to fill subsequent or similar full time, part time, and casual vacancies.

Salary

$76,849 to $82,996 per annum. Our Employer 12% superannuation contribution is on top of this amount.

Salary range is in accordance with the Health and Human Services (Tasmanian State Service) Award (HAHSA) and the Public Sector Union Wages Agreement (PSUWA).

Benefits available to eligible candidates 

A range of leave entitlements, access to additional leave incentives, generous personal leave, including family incentives, purchased leave options.

Workplace flexibility aligned our flexible work policy.

Fitness Passport - You, and your family can access 40+ fitness facilities across Tasmania for just $14.50 per week per person, or $28.05 for a family.

Carer Employer Accreditation, evidencing our commitment to supporting employees with caring responsibilities. (Find out more under the Carer Recognition Act 2023).
